definitions.explanation: The screen of a device on which information is shown to the user — for example the panel of a smartphone, the monitor of a PC, or the LCD readout of an appliance. Often used in technical manuals and UI documentation to refer to whatever layout is currently visible on the screen.

examples.japanese: {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}が{暗|くら}い。
{表示画面|ひょうじがめん}にエラーメッセージが{出|で}た。
examples.english: An error message appeared on the display screen.

examples.japanese: {設定|せってい}を{変|か}えると{表示画面|ひょうじがめん}のレイアウトが{切|き}り{替|か}わる。
examples.english: When you change the settings, the layout of the display screen switches accordingly.

notes:
Compound of {表示|ひょうじ} ('display; indication') and {画面|がめん} ('screen'). Used in technical contexts — device manuals, software documentation, UI design — to refer to the currently visible screen or screen layout, as opposed to the physical hardware panel.

USAGE:
- Often refers to the logical content shown on the screen (a window, menu, or view), not just the physical surface.
- Frequently appears with verbs like {切|き}り{替|か}わる ('to switch'), {表示|ひょうじ}される ('to be displayed'), or {更新|こうしん}される ('to be updated').
- In user manuals, directions like 「{表示画面|ひょうじがめん}の{指示|しじ}に{従|したが}ってください」 ('Follow the instructions on the display') are common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}を{確認|かくにん}する: to check the display screen
- {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}が{切|き}り{替|か}わる: the display screen switches
- {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}に{表示|ひょうじ}される: to be shown on the display screen
- {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}の{設定|せってい}: display screen settings
- {表示画面|ひょうじがめん}が{消|き}える: the display screen goes blank

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {画面|がめん}: screen — the everyday, general word; {表示画面|ひょうじがめん} sounds more technical and specifies the display function.
- ディスプレイ: display — loanword used especially for computer monitors or standalone displays.
- モニター: monitor — usually a standalone computer or video monitor; a hardware term.
- {液晶画面|えきしょうがめん}: LCD screen — specifies the panel technology; contrast with {有機|ゆうき}EL{画面|がめん} (OLED screen).
- {表示|ひょうじ}: display; indication — the base word; on its own, covers any kind of shown indication, not just a screen.
